chapter: Looking back, big bands and sidemen
title: Nistico's European work and place in the Herds
summary: Wong mentions a German big band album with Nistico; both agree he set a model as a swinger, while Herbert's value lay in other facets.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I just heard an album about a month ago, that was put together by some German. And Mike Baron that Sal was playing -- it was a big band, I don't know what it's all about, there wasn't much background on it. But it was while he was over there.
Or whether he was just in and out or whether --
It might have been like a workshop band or it might been a working group.
Yeah, yeah. It was this British player, Alan Skidmore, that was playing, a saxophone player. Yeah, I think that Sal was a pretty prominent figure in the annals of the Herds.
In his work, and he kind of set a model for many players, maybe in the band's mind, too, that, 'Boy, we need a swinger like that.'
That's right, that -- and carry the ball at any speed.
Uh-huh, because Gregory did a magnificent job in carrying many of those kinds of responsibilities, but he had more.
Yeah, it was his other facets that were really more important, I thought, his ballad facets and doubles and so on.
